core_obligations: Part (1) (proof line 7541): an isomorphism X' -> X is in particular an open covering, and open coverings are qc coverings by the remark preceding the lemma.

Part (2), refinement of a qc covering by qc coverings (proof lines 7544-7562): for a point x choose finitely many i_a and quasi-compact E_a inside X_{i_a} whose images form a neighbourhood of x; for each e in E_a choose finitely many j and quasi-compact F_{e,j} whose images cover a neighbourhood of e; quasi-compactness of E_a makes finitely many e_k suffice, and the resulting finite union of the f_i(g_{ij}(F_{e_k,j})) is a neighbourhood of x.

Part (3), base change of a qc covering (proof lines 7565-7574): for x' in X' with image x, choose finitely many quasi-compact E_j inside X_{i_j} covering a neighbourhood of x, then a quasi-compact neighbourhood F of x' mapping into that neighbourhood; each F x_X E_j is quasi-compact and F is the image of their coproduct, so the base change is a qc covering.
Note that the counted proof establishes exactly the three axioms needed for a pretopology, in the order in which they are stated.
proof_roadmap: Part (1) is immediate from open coverings being qc coverings.
For part (2), start from the neighbourhood data for x, refine each E_a by finitely many F_{e,j} using quasi-compactness of E_a, and read off a finite neighbourhood of x for the composite family.
For part (3), pull the finite neighbourhood data back along x' and use a quasi-compact neighbourhood F of x', with the fibre products F x_X E_j quasi-compact and F as their image.
All three parts are the axioms making qc coverings a topology on LC.
difficulty_reason: The lemma verifies the three axioms of a pretopology for the qc coverings on the category LC of Hausdorff locally quasi-compact spaces (statement lines 7524-7538). The non-formal content is in parts (2) and (3), which are finite-refinement arguments: in part (2) one first chooses finitely many quasi-compact E_a whose images cover a neighbourhood of x, then refines each by finitely many quasi-compact F_{e,j}, using quasi-compactness of E_a to cut the e-parameter down to finitely many points (proof lines 7544-7562); in part (3) one pulls back the finite data along the base change and uses a quasi-compact neighbourhood F of x' whose fibre products with the E_j are quasi-compact, with F the image of their coproduct (proof lines 7565-7574). The claim is H2: two explicit finite-refinement constructions after one immediate part.
